items.title: Data shows why Australians are stuck and not switching jobs or starting businesses
items.description: People are less mobile, less dynamic and more risk-averse than we used to be, a series of economic indicators shows.

items.title: Trump's deal-making leaves Iran in the driver's seat and Israel more vulnerable
items.description: Israel goes from looking like the new regional hegemon to looking like it is under greater threat now than it has in years, while Iran now has room to rebuild its proxies.

items.title: First Australian activist detained from Gaza flotilla returns home
items.description: Gemma O'Toole is the first of 11 Australian activists detained by Israel off the Gaza-bound Global Sumud Flotilla to arrive back in Australia.

items.title: With an Iran deal looming, Republicans are turning on each other
items.description: The US president says he "won't be rushed" to announce the details, but already critics and Iran are suggesting he has lost the negotiations.

items.title: Live: Steggall confirms talks underway for teals to form new political party
items.description: Independent MP Zali Steggall says she is open to the teals forming their own political party but declines to say how far talks have progressed. Follow live.

items.title: The migration maths behind the housing crisis is not what politicians claim
items.description: Arthur Calwell argued migration was essential to national survival. Today, the Coalition says it should depend on how many homes get built, but the economics are far from straightforward.

items.title: Top spy boss first witness as antisemitism royal commission resumes
items.description: The head of Australia's spy agency will be the first witness when the royal commission on antisemitism resumes this week.

items.title: Coronial inquests into police shooting and Dezi Freeman death to begin
items.description: Two separate directions hearings will be heard in the Coroners Court of Victoria before State Coroner Judge Liberty Sanger, who will oversee the structure and scope of the inquests.

items.title: 'It's atrocious, the apathy': Survivor calls on governments to act
items.description: At nine years old, Bronwyn was sent to a notorious government-run children's home without her parents' consent. What unfolded next impacted the rest of her life.

items.title: Link between terrorism and DV could be key to preventing homicide
items.description: A world-first research project is aiming to prevent family and intimate partner homicides with similar strategies to those being used to tackle terrorism and lone-actor attacks.

items.title: Trump's push for a ceasefire is good for peace but our wallets still feel the pain
items.description: US President Donald Trump was yesterday touting an end to the war in Iran, but declaring mission accomplished in Washington will not spare Australian consumers, and politicians, from the economic fallout of the conflict.

items.title: No Ferry McFerryface: New name for Sydney suburb won't be by popular vote
items.description: In the coming weeks Sydneysiders will be asked to help rename Bays West, while a competition will open to decide the "look and feel" of the future suburb.

items.title: Live: ASX 200 set to fall despite Dow closing at record high, oil drops
items.description: The Australian share market is expected to fall, with ASX 200 futures pointing to a negative start to the week. That comes despite the Dow Jones hitting new records and as the price of Brent Crude oil drops under $US100 a barrel. Follow our live business blog.

items.title: Australia's opening times are world leading and researchers say it's a strength
items.description: Australia has a "distinctive strength" when it comes to early trading, but more knowledge is needed for businesses to fully capitalise on it.

items.title: A movie about mystery-hunting sheep delights this May
items.description: Plus the rom-com of yore returns in Finding Emily, the farmyard mystery that's been delighting audiences, and a gory Hollywood video game adaptation filmed on the Gold Coast.

items.title: What life is like without alcohol
items.description: Here's what you had to say about leaving alcohol behind and how it's impacted your health, friendships and lifestyle.

items.title: Quiz: Will you land a knockout punch on this week's history round?

items.title: Victim-survivor says her fight for justice was worth it despite court's ruling
items.description: The Canberra woman says the justice system is unpredictable for victim-survivors but many aspects are worth it.

items.title: Scientist 'shocked' $300m irrigation scheme pushing ahead without studies
items.description: A $300 million irrigation scheme will supply 37.2 gigalitres of water to farming areas near Hobart from 2030. A scientists fears the taxpayer-funded scheme could put a major river at risk.

items.title: Head of Victoria's new childcare watchdog vows to protect kids

items.title: Farmers fight battery storage proposals on agricultural land

items.title: Man charged with attempted murder and arson after double stabbing and house fire in Raceview
items.description: Police were called to an altercation at an Ipswich address on Sunday afternoon.

items.title: Man killed in alleged hit-and-run on Perth freeway, accused driver charged
items.description: A 22-year-old man dies after being struck by a car in an alleged hit-and-run on the Mitchell Freeway in Perth's north, with police charging another man who they say later gave himself up.

items.title: Vegemite banned, Tim Tams welcome: Baseballer brings Aussie flavour to US

items.title: When and how to watch State of Origin Game I between the Blues and Maroons
items.description: Game I of the men's 2026 State of Origin series will be held this Wednesday at Sydney's Stadium Australia. Here's what to know about the match.
